config.title: flex-wrap and gap

intro.title: flex-wrap and gap
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a flexible photo gallery layout that automatically adjusts to fit different screen sizes. You will learn how to use the CSS flex-wrap property to control whether flex items wrap onto new lines or stay in a single row. Additionally, you will apply the gap property to create consistent spacing between the gallery items without using margins. This lesson focuses on practical CSS layout techniques using Flexbox to create responsive and visually balanced designs.
intro.usecase: The flex-wrap and gap properties are essential for creating responsive card layouts and navigation systems that adapt to different screen sizes. In e-commerce product grids, flex-wrap allows items to flow into multiple rows when space is limited, while gap provides consistent spacing between products without messy margin calculations. Developers use these properties in dashboard widgets, social media feeds, and filter tag collections where content needs to reflow gracefully. This pattern appears in interfaces like Pinterest's masonry layout, Shopify's product listings, and Netflix's movie rows that wrap on mobile devices.

objectives: Apply flex-wrap to control how flex items flow across multiple lines
Configure gap properties to create consistent spacing between flex items
Implement responsive layouts by adjusting flex-wrap based on container width
Construct multi-line flex containers with proper alignment using wrap-reverse
Manipulate both row-gap and column-gap to fine-tune spacing in two dimensions
Integrate flex-wrap with other flex properties to create complex layouts
Initialize flex containers with appropriate wrap behavior for different content types
Update existing flex layouts by adding gap spacing without breaking alignment

steps.title: Set fixed widths on flex items to create overflow
steps.instruction: Add a width property to your flex item rule to make each item 200px wide, which will cause them to overflow the container.
steps.hint: Use the width property with a value of 200px inside the flex item rule.
steps.expectedOutcome: The flex items will now each be 200px wide, causing them to overflow the container horizontally when there are multiple items.
successCriteria: The flex item rule includes a width property set to 200px.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've added a width property with the value 200px to your flex item rule.
steps.feedbackWrong: The flex items don't have the required width property. Add 'width: 200px;' to your flex item rule.

steps.title: Observe the default nowrap behavior
steps.instruction: Preview your layout in the browser to see how flex items shrink to fit within the container width by default.
steps.hint: The flex container's default flex-wrap value is 'nowrap', which forces all items onto a single line even if they overflow.

steps.expectedOutcome: You'll see all flex items compressed onto one row, with some items potentially shrinking or overflowing the container.
successCriteria: Preview shows flex items arranged in a single row with visible compression/overflow
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure to preview the layout to see how the items behave when they don't all fit in one row.
steps.feedbackWrong: The goal is to observe the current layout behavior - preview your CSS to see how flex items arrange themselves by default.

steps.title: Apply flex-wrap: wrap to allow multi-line layout
steps.instruction: Add the flex-wrap: wrap property to your container rule to allow flex items to wrap onto multiple lines when they don't fit horizontally.
steps.hint: Look for the CSS rule that defines your flex container and add flex-wrap: wrap; inside it.
steps.expectedOutcome: The flex container will now allow items to wrap to new lines when the container width is insufficient.
successCriteria: The container rule includes flex-wrap: wrap;
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you've added flex-wrap: wrap; to the correct CSS rule (the container rule).
steps.feedbackWrong: The container rule doesn't have flex-wrap: wrap; yet. Add this property to allow items to wrap.

steps.title: Observe the wrapped layout
steps.instruction: Preview the layout in the browser to see how the items now wrap to new lines instead of overflowing.
steps.hint: Open the preview panel or browser to visually confirm the wrapped layout.
steps.analogousExample: /* After applying flex-wrap: wrap, items will wrap to new lines when they exceed the container width */
steps.expectedOutcome: You should see the flex items wrapping to multiple lines within the container.
successCriteria: The layout preview shows items wrapping to new lines instead of overflowing.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: preview the layout in the browser to observe the wrapping behavior.
steps.feedbackWrong: The layout should show items wrapping to new lines. Check if flex-wrap: wrap is applied correctly.

steps.title: Add gap property to create spacing between items
steps.instruction: Add a gap property to your flex container rule to create consistent spacing between the flex items.
steps.hint: Use the gap property inside your container selector. You can specify a value like 10px or 1rem.
steps.expectedOutcome: The flex container will have a gap property applied, creating spacing between items in both rows and columns.
successCriteria: The container rule includes a gap property with a valid CSS length value.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added the gap property, but make sure it has a valid value like 10px or 1rem.
steps.feedbackWrong: The gap property is missing or incorrect. Add it to the container rule with a spacing value.

steps.title: Observe the combined effect of flex-wrap and gap
steps.instruction: Set a specific value for the gap property in your .container rule to create visible spacing between items.
steps.hint: Add a numeric value with a unit like 'px' or 'rem' after 'gap:' in your .container rule.
steps.expectedOutcome: The flex items will wrap to new lines when needed, with consistent spacing between them both horizontally and vertically.
successCriteria: The .container rule includes a numeric gap value with a unit (e.g., 20px).
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your gap value includes a unit (like px or rem).
steps.feedbackWrong: Try adding a specific numeric value with a unit (e.g., 20px) after 'gap:' in the .container rule.

steps.title: Experiment with different gap values
steps.instruction: Change the gap value in your .container rule to a different number (e.g., 40px) to see how spacing changes.
steps.hint: Look for the gap property in your .container rule and modify its value.
steps.expectedOutcome: The spacing between flex items increases when you use a larger gap value, demonstrating how gap controls both row and column spacing in a flex-wrap layout.
successCriteria: The .container rule has a gap property with a value different from 20px.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've modified the gap value, but try using a different number like 40px or 10px to see more noticeable changes.
steps.feedbackWrong: Make sure you're modifying the gap property value in the .container rule, not creating a new rule.

steps.title: Try flex-wrap: wrap-reverse
steps.instruction: In your .container rule, change the flex-wrap property value from 'wrap' to 'wrap-reverse'.
steps.hint: Look for the flex-wrap property in your .container CSS rule and modify its value.
steps.expectedOutcome: The flex items will wrap onto multiple lines in reverse order, starting from the bottom or right depending on the flex direction.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've changed the flex-wrap property value in the .container rule to 'wrap-reverse'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The flex-wrap property in the .container rule should be set to 'wrap-reverse'.
